sentences.dutch: Ik woon in een groot huis.
sentences.english: I live in a big house.

note: Sounds like 'house' - same Germanic root. Dutch kept the 'ui' sound where English shifted to 'ou'.
Identical to English 'water'. One of the easiest Dutch words!

sentences.english: What do you want to eat?

note: Sounds like 'eaten'. It means both 'to eat' and 'food'.

sentences.english: Do you want something to drink?

note: Sounds like 'drink-en'. Just add -en to the English word.
Sounds like 'gone' without the 'ne'. Where did he go? He's gaan!
Think 'come in!' - komen is just 'come' with -en.
Sounds like 'haben' in German. Think 'I have to heb it!'
Zijn means both 'to be' and 'his'. 'Hij is blij met zijn hond' = He is happy with his dog. Two words in English, one in Dutch.
Related to English 'will' as in 'willpower'. You will what you want. Willen = to want.
Same root as English 'can'. German also has können. The K sound stayed in Dutch and German but English softened it.
Same root as English 'must'. German has müssen. The -oeten ending is distinctly Dutch.
Think 'mogul' - someone with power who is allowed to do things. Mogen = may/to be allowed.
Related to English 'see' through old Germanic. The z- in Dutch often maps to s- in English.
Same root as English 'hear'. Dutch kept the h-, just added -en.
Related to English 'wit' as in 'wisdom'. If you have wit, you weten things.
Related to English 'ken' (Scottish for 'know'). Kennen is knowing a person, weten is knowing a fact.

sentences.dutch: Ik denk dat het goed is.

note: Same root as English 'think'. The d/th swap is common between Dutch and English.
Same root as English 'say'. Dutch z often corresponds to English s.
Same root as German 'fragen'. The v/f swap is typical Dutch-German.
Same root as English 'give'. Dutch g often maps to English g, the rest shifted over time.
Same root as English 'name' through old Germanic 'neman' (to take).
Same root as English 'make'. Almost identical!
Same root as English 'work'. German has 'werken' too. The whole Germanic family shares this word.
Same root as English 'learn'. Identical meaning, just add -en.
Schrijven shares roots with English 'scribe' and 'script' through Latin 'scribere'.
Same root as English 'lesson' through Latin 'legere' (to read).
Same root as English 'speak'. The spr- beginning stayed the same across centuries.
Combines 'be-' with grijpen (to grasp). To understand is to 'grasp' an idea!
Same root as English 'find'. Also means 'to think/have an opinion' - ik vind het leuk = I find it nice.
Same root as English 'seek'. Zoeken = to seek/search.
Dag means 'day' but also 'hello' and 'goodbye' - like saying 'good day!' for greeting and parting.
Identical to English 'week'. Same word, same meaning.
Same root as English 'month' and 'moon'. Maand = moon-time.
Same root as English 'year'. German has 'Jahr'. The j/y swap is common.
Same root as English 'tide' (as in time/season). 'Time and tide wait for no man.'
Same root as English 'hour'. From Latin 'hora'.
Same as English 'minute'. From Latin 'minutum'.
Identical to English 'man'. Same word since ancient Germanic.
Same root as German 'Frau'. Means both 'woman' and 'wife'.
Same root as English 'kind' (as in 'kindergarten'). Kind = child.
Same root as English 'father'. The v/f swap is standard Dutch-English.
Same root as English 'mother'. Dutch moeder, German Mutter, English mother - all from the same root.

sentences.english: My son is ten years old.

note: Same root as English 'son'. Almost identical.
Same root as English 'daughter'. Dutch dochter, German Tochter.
Same root as English 'friend'. Vriend and friend share the same ancient Germanic origin.
Same root as English 'book'. German has 'Buch'. Originally meant 'beech tree' (writing tablets were beech wood).
Short for 'automobiel', same as English 'auto/automobile'.
No English equivalent - the bicycle is deeply Dutch! Fiets may come from 'vitesse' (French for speed).
Same as English 'train'. From French.
Identical to English 'school'. From Greek 'scholē' (leisure, learning).
Same root as English 'work'. Werk is the noun form.
Same root as English 'gold/yield'. Money was originally gold. German 'Geld' is identical.
Same root as English 'stead' (as in 'farmstead'). A stad is a place that stays = city.

sentences.english: The Netherlands is a small country.

note: Identical to English 'land'.
Same as English 'coffee'. From Arabic 'qahwa' through Turkish.
Same as English 'tea'. Both from Chinese 'chá'.
Same root as English 'way'. A weg is a way/road.
Same root as English 'street'. From Latin 'strata'.
Same root as English 'door'. Almost identical.
Same root as English 'hound'. English shifted to 'dog', but 'hound' preserved the old word.
Same root as English 'cat'. Nearly identical across all Germanic languages.
Same root as English 'great'. Groot = great/big.
Same root as English 'clean' through old Germanic. The meaning shifted from 'pure/small' to 'clean' in English.
Same root as English 'good'. Nearly identical.
Related to German 'schlecht'. Think 'slight' - something slight is not good.
No direct English cousin. Mooi is uniquely Dutch - sounds like 'moy', think 'oh my, how beautiful!'
Uniquely Dutch! No English equivalent. Lekker covers 'tasty, nice, comfortable' - the Dutch love this word.
Identical to English 'warm'.
Same root as English 'cold'. The k/c swap is typical Dutch-English.
Same root as English 'new'. German 'neu'. The ni-/ne- beginning is shared.
Same root as English 'old'. German 'alt'. The ou-/ol- shift is regular.
Same root as English 'young'. German 'jung'. Nearly identical.
Same root as English 'long'. Means both 'long' and 'tall'.
Same root as English 'curt/short'. The k/c swap again.
No direct English relative but think 'snail mail is not snel!'
Think 'blithe' (English for cheerful/happy). Same root - blij = blithe = happy.
The '-lijk' ending is like English '-ly'. Opposite of moeilijk (difficult).
Comes from moeite (effort). Something difficult takes effort! Opposite of makkelijk.
Same as English 'interesting'. From Latin 'interesse'.
Same root as English 'dear' (expensive). 'That costs a dear price' = duur.
Same root as English 'what'. The w- beginning stayed.
Same root as English 'who'. Wie = who.
Same root as English 'where'. Waar = where.
Wan + neer. Same root as English 'when'. Wanneer just has an extra syllable.
Waar (where/true) + om (around). Literally 'where-around' = why.
Same root as English 'how'. Nearly identical.
Hoe (how) + veel (much). Literally 'how much'.

sentences.dutch: Ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek ben.
sentences.english: I stay home because I'm sick.

note: Om (around) + dat (that). Literally 'around that' = because.

sentences.dutch: Ik wil wel, maar ik kan niet.
sentences.english: I want to, but I can't.

sentences.dutch: Ik wil komen, maar ik kan niet.
sentences.english: I want to come, but I can't.

note: Maar means 'but' and also 'only/just'. 'Maar één' = only/just one. Two meanings, one tiny word.

sentences.english: My friend and I are going.

note: Same root as English 'and'. One of the most basic shared Germanic words.

sentences.english: Do you want coffee or tea?

note: Same root as English 'or' (through old Germanic). Identical meaning.

sentences.dutch: Als het regent, blijf ik thuis.
sentences.english: If it rains, I stay home.

note: Same root as English 'as/also'. Als can mean 'if', 'when', or 'as'.
Same root as English 'than/then'. Dan serves both meanings in Dutch.
Same root as English 'now'. German 'nun'. Very old shared word.
Al (all) + tijd (time). Literally 'all-time' = always.

sentences.dutch: Ik ben nooit in Japan geweest.

note: Think 'no it!' - nooit = never. Actually from 'no' + 'ooit' (ever).

sentences.dutch: Soms ga ik naar de film.
sentences.english: Sometimes I go to the movies.

note: Think 'some-s' = sometimes.

sentences.dutch: Ik ga vaak naar de bioscoop.
sentences.english: I often go to the cinema.

note: No direct English cousin, but think 'I'm a vaak visitor' = I come often.
Same root as English 'here'. Nearly identical.
Same root as English 'there'. Nearly identical.
Same root as English 'well'. Means 'indeed' or emphasizes something - 'ik wil wel' = I do want to.
Same root as English 'not' (through 'naught/nought'). Dutch niet, German nicht.
Same root as English 'eke' (old English for 'also'). Think 'ook = too'.
Same root as English 'enough' (oddly!). Through old Germanic 'nōg'.
Al means both 'already' and 'all'. 'Ik heb al gegeten' = already eaten. 'Al mijn vrienden' = all my friends.
Same root as English 'whole/heal'. Heel means 'very' but originally meant 'whole'.

sentences.english: I have a lot of work.

note: Same root as English 'full' through old Germanic. Veel = much/many.
Same root as English 'wee' (small). Weinig = a wee bit.
Same root as English 'I' through old Germanic 'ik/ich'. German still uses 'ich'.
Informal 'you'. Same root as English 'ye' (old English for you).
Same root as English 'he'. Nearly identical.
Same root as English 'she'. Also means 'they'. Context tells you which.
Same root as English 'we'. Nearly identical.
Same root as English 'you all' or 'y'all'. The plural you.
Same root as English 'mine/my'. Mijn = my.
Same root as English 'your'. Jouw = your (informal).
Van (from) + daag (day). Literally 'from this day' = today.
Same root as English 'morrow/morning'. Tomorrow in English is literally 'to-morrow'.
Gister (yester) + en. Same root as English 'yesterday'.
Te (at) + huis (house). Literally 'at house' = at home.
Same root as English 'bout' (as in 'about'). Buiten = outside.
Same root as English 'bin/within'. Binnen = inside/within.
Same root as English 'trug' is not a word, but think 'retro/return'. Terug = back.
Same root as English 'same'. Samen = together (being the same/united).
Same root as English 'all' + 'one'. Alleen = all-one = alone.
Mis (miss) + schien (shine/seem). Literally 'it may seem' = maybe.

sentences.english: Of course I want to come.

note: Literally 'naturally' from natuur (nature). When something is natural, of course it happens!
From eigen (own). What something 'actually' is, is what it truly/own-ly is.
Think 'alas!' - helaas means unfortunately. Very similar feeling.
From geluk (luck/happiness). Add 'on-' for the opposite: ongelukkig (unhappy).
Identical to English 'in'.

sentences.dutch: Het boek ligt op de tafel.
sentences.english: The book is on the table.

note: Op means 'on' but also 'up' and 'finished/used up'. 'De melk is op' = the milk is finished.
Same root as English 'with' (through old Germanic 'mid/met').
Voor means 'for' and 'before/in front of'. 'Voor jou' = for you. 'Voor het huis' = in front of the house.
Same root as English 'near'. Naar = to (direction).
Same root as English 'of/from'. Van = of/from.
Aan means 'at/to' but also 'on' (activated). 'Het licht is aan' = the light is on.
Bij means 'at/near' but also 'with'. 'Bij mijn ouders' = with/at my parents. Also means 'bee' (de bij)!
Uit means 'out of/from' but also 'off'. 'Het licht is uit' = the light is off. Opposite of aan.
Same root as English 'through/door'. A door is what you go through!
Over means 'about' and 'over', but also 'left over'. 'Er is niets over' = nothing is left over.
Same root as English 'to' (as in 'up to'). Tot = until.

sentences.dutch: Na het eten ga ik slapen.
sentences.english: After eating I go to sleep.

note: Same root as English 'nigh' (near/after). Na = after.

sentences.dutch: De kat zit onder de tafel.
sentences.english: The cat sits under the table.

note: Same root as English 'under'. Nearly identical.

sentences.dutch: De lamp hangt boven de tafel.
sentences.english: The lamp hangs above the table.

note: Same root as English 'above' (through old Germanic 'boven/above').

sentences.dutch: Het huis staat tussen twee bomen.
sentences.english: The house stands between two trees.

note: Same root as English 'betwixt/between'. Tussen = between.
Zonder = without. Think 'sunder' (old English for 'apart/asunder').
Same root as English 'against' (through old Germanic). Tegen = against.
Same root as English 'since'. Nearly identical.

sentences.dutch: Tijdens de les moet je luisteren.

note: Tijdens = during. Literally 'at the time of'.
Same root as English 'one'. Dutch één, German eins.
Same root as English 'two'. Dutch twee, German zwei.
Same root as English 'three'. Dutch drie, German drei.
Same root as English 'four'. Dutch vier, German vier.
Same root as English 'five'. Dutch vijf, German fünf.
Same root as English 'six'. Nearly identical.

sentences.dutch: Er zijn zeven dagen in een week.
sentences.english: There are seven days in a week.

note: Same root as English 'seven'. Dutch zeven, German sieben.

sentences.dutch: Ik werk acht uur per dag.
sentences.english: I work eight hours per day.

note: Same root as English 'eight'. Dutch acht, German acht.

sentences.dutch: De les begint om negen uur.
sentences.english: The class starts at nine o'clock.

note: Same root as English 'nine'. Dutch negen, German neun.
Same root as English 'ten'. Dutch tien, German zehn.
Same root as English 'lope' (to run with long strides). Lopen = to walk.
Same root as English 'sit'. Zitten = to sit. The z/s swap is standard.
Same root as English 'stand'. Staan = to stand.

sentences.english: The book lies on the table.

note: Same root as English 'lie' (to lie down). Liggen = lie.
Same root as English 'sleep'. Slapen = to sleep. Almost identical.
Same root as English 'won' (to dwell). 'Wont' means 'accustomed to living'. Wonen = to live.
Same root as English 'believe' (through old Germanic 'belīfan'). Blijven = to stay/remain.
Same root as English 'watch/wait'. The w- stayed, meaning shifted slightly.

sentences.english: I want to buy a car.

note: Same root as German 'kaufen'. English 'cheap' comes from the same family (a good deal/trade).
Kopen means 'to buy'. Add 'ver-' and it flips to selling - buying away from yourself!
Same root as English 'pay' through old French. Dutch betalen, be- is a prefix + talen (to count).
Think 'peekIn' - kijken = to look/watch.
Same root as English 'listen'. Luisteren is just the Dutch version.
Same root as English 'play' (through old Germanic). Spelen = to play.
Same root as German 'kriegen'. Think 'I krijg what I deserve' = I get.
Same root as English 'bring'. Identical meaning.
Same root as English 'haul/hale'. Halen = to fetch/get.

sentences.dutch: Ik leg het boek op tafel.
sentences.english: I put the book on the table.
Put the book on the table.

note: Same root as English 'lay'. Leggen = to lay/put.

sentences.english: Put the cup on the table.

note: Same root as English 'set'. Zetten = to put/set. The z/s swap again.
Same root as English 'ride'. Rijden = to drive/ride.
Same root as English 'fly'. Vliegen = to fly. The v/f swap.
Same root as English 'swim'. Zwemmen = to swim. The zw/sw swap.
Same root as English 'stop'. Nearly identical.

sentences.dutch: De les begint om negen uur.

note: Same root as English 'begin'. Nearly identical.
From Latin 'probare' (to test). Same root as English 'probe/prove'. Proberen = to try.
Same root as English 'help'. Nearly identical.
The 'ver-' prefix often means 'away' or 'completely'. Opposite of herinneren (remember).
The 'her-' means 'again' and 'inner' is inside. To remember is to bring something back inside your mind!
Same root as English 'feel'. Voelen = to feel. The v/f swap.
Same root as English 'believe' (through old Germanic 'galaubjan'). Ge-loven = believe.
Same root as English 'hope'. Nearly identical.

sentences.dutch: Ik verwacht je om drie uur.

note: Ver (far/thoroughly) + wachten (wait). To 'wait thoroughly' = to expect.

sentences.english: I want to win the match.

note: Same root as English 'win'. Winnen = to win.
Ver (away) + liezen (lose). Same root as English 'lose' with a prefix.
Contains 'ander' which means 'other'. To change something is to make it other/different!
Same root as English 'choose'. Kiezen = choose. The k/ch swap.
From French 'décider'. Beslissen is the Dutch version of 'decide'.
Same root as English 'open'. Nearly identical.

sentences.dutch: De winkel sluit om zes uur.

note: Same root as English 'slot' (a lock/closure). Sluiten = to close/shut.
Same root as English 'steer' (to direct/send). Sturen = to send.

sentences.english: The food is on the table.

note: Same root as English 'table' through Latin 'tabula'. Tafel = table.
Same root as English 'stool'. A stoel is a chair (upgraded stool!).
Identical to English 'bed'.
Same root as English 'chamber'. Kamer = room.
Same root as English 'kitchen'. Keuken = kitchen. From Latin 'coquina'.
Same root as English 'town' (through old Germanic for 'enclosed space'). Tuin = garden.
No direct English cousin. Think 'raam-frame' around a window.
Same root as English 'sun'. Zon = sun.
Same root as English 'moon'. Maan = moon.
Same root as English 'rain'. Regen = rain.
Identical to English 'wind'.
Same root as English 'snow'. Sneeuw = snow.
Same root as English 'beam' (a tree/wood). Boom = tree.
Same root as English 'bloom'. Bloem = flower. A flower is something that blooms.
Same root as English 'sea'. Zee = sea. The z/s swap.
Same root as English 'berg' (as in iceberg). Berg = mountain.

sentences.dutch: Ik wandel graag in het bos.
sentences.english: I like to walk in the forest.

note: Bos means 'forest' but also 'bunch/bouquet'. 'Een bos bloemen' = a bunch of flowers.
Same as English 'photo'. Short for 'fotografie'.
Same as English 'film'.
Same as English 'music' through Latin 'musica'. Muziek = music.
Same root as English 'fragile' (Latin 'frangere'). Actually from Germanic - a vraag 'breaks' the silence.
Ant means 'back/against' and woord means 'word'. An answer is a word back!
Same as English 'problem' through Latin/Greek.
Same as English 'idea' through Greek.
Contains halen (to fetch). A story is something you 'fetch' from memory and recount!
Same root as old English 'brief' (a letter/document). A brief is a short letter.
Same as English 'telephone'. Telefoon = telephone.
Same as English 'computer'.
Same root as English 'rise' (to journey). A reis is a trip you rise up to take.
From French 'vacance'. Same root as English 'vacation/vacancy'.
Same root as English 'feast'. Feest = party/celebration.

sentences.dutch: Dit is een cadeau voor jou.
sentences.english: This is a present for you.

note: From French 'cadeau'. No English equivalent - think 'a gift cad-owed to you'.
Same root as English 'price/prize'. Prijs covers both meanings.
Related to German 'Winkel' (shop). Think 'twinkle' in a shop window.
Same as English 'restaurant'. From French.
Same as English 'hotel'. From French.

sentences.dutch: De trein vertrekt van het station.
sentences.english: The train leaves from the station.

note: Same as English 'station'.
Same as English 'bus'.
Vlieg means 'fly' and tuig means 'craft' or 'gear'. A fly-craft!
Same root as English 'color' through Latin 'color'. Kleur = color.
Same root as English 'red'. Rood = red. German 'rot'.
Same root as English 'blue' through old Germanic 'blāwaz'.
Same root as English 'green'. Groen = green.
Same root as English 'yellow' through old Germanic. Geel = yellow.
Same root as English 'white'. Wit = white.
Same root as English 'swart' (archaic for black). Zwart = black.
Maan (moon) + dag (day). Monday = Moon-day in English too!
Named after the Norse god Tyr. Tuesday = Tyr's day, Dinsdag = Thing's day (Norse assembly).
Named after the god Wodan (Odin). Wednesday = Woden's day, Woensdag = Wodan's day.
Named after Thor (Donar). Thursday = Thor's day, Donderdag = Donar's day. Donder = thunder!
Named after the goddess Frigg. Friday = Frigg's day, Vrijdag = Vrij's day.
Named after Saturn. Saturday has Saturn, Zaterdag comes from Latin 'Saturni dies' too.
Zon (sun) + dag (day). Sunday = Sun-day in English too!
Same as English 'January'. From Latin 'Januarius'.
Same as English 'February'. From Latin 'Februarius'.
Same as English 'March'. From Latin 'Martius'.
Same as English 'April'. From Latin 'Aprilis'.
Same as English 'May'. From Latin 'Maius'.

sentences.dutch: In juni is het lang licht.
sentences.english: In June it's light for a long time.

note: Same as English 'June'. From Latin 'Junius'.
Same as English 'July'. From Latin 'Julius'.

sentences.dutch: Ik ga op vakantie in augustus.
sentences.english: I go on vacation in August.

note: Same as English 'August'. From Latin 'Augustus'.
Same as English 'September'.
Same as English 'October'.
Same as English 'November'.
Same as English 'December'.

sentences.dutch: In de lente bloeien de bloemen.

note: Think 'Lent' (the spring church season). Lente = spring.
Same root as English 'summer'. Zomer = summer.

sentences.dutch: De bladeren vallen in de herfst.

note: Same root as English 'harvest'. Herfst = autumn. Autumn was harvest time.
Same as English 'winter'.
Think 'ochtend' starts with 'och' like 'o'clock' in the morning.
Mid (middle) + dag (day). Literally 'mid-day' = afternoon.
Same root as English 'evening'. Avond = evening.
Same root as English 'night'. Nacht = night. German 'Nacht'.
Same root as English 'head'. Hoofd = head. The -oo- maps to English -ea-.
Identical to English 'hand'.
Same root as English 'foot'. Voet = foot. The v/f swap.
Same root as English 'eye' (through old Germanic 'augō'). Oog = eye.
Same root as English 'ear'. Oor = ear.
Same root as English 'mouth'. Mond = mouth.
Same root as English 'nose'. Neus = nose.

sentences.dutch: Ik hou van je met heel mijn hart.
sentences.english: I love you with all my heart.

note: Same root as English 'heart'. Hart = heart.
Lichaam = li (limb/body) + chaam (shape). Think 'like-a-body'.
Gezicht means 'face' but also 'sight/vision'. Related to zien (to see) - your face is what's seen.
Haar means both 'hair' and 'her'. Same root as English 'hair'. Context tells you which: 'haar haar' = her hair!
Same root as English 'ridge' (back of something). Rug = back.
Been means both 'leg' and 'bone'. Related to English 'bone'. Context tells you which.
Arm means both 'arm' (body part) and 'poor'. Same root as English 'arm'. The 'poor' meaning may come from having empty arms.
Same as English 'doctor'. From Latin 'doctor'.
Zieken (sick people) + huis (house). A 'sick-house' = hospital.
Same root as English 'medicine'. From Latin 'medicina'.
Same root as German 'siech' (sick). Think 'seeking a doctor when you're ziek'.
Related to English 'sound' as in 'safe and sound'. Both mean healthy!
Same root as English 'moody' (tired/emotional). Moe = tired.
Same root as English 'hunger'. Honger = hunger.
Same root as English 'thirst'. Dorst = thirst. The d/th swap.
Same root as English 'bread'. Brood = bread.
Same root as English 'milk'. Melk = milk.
Same root as English 'cheese' through Latin 'caseus'. Kaas = cheese.
Same root as English 'egg'. Ei = egg. Short and sweet.
Same root as English 'flesh'. Vlees = meat/flesh. The v/f swap.
Same root as English 'fish'. Vis = fish. The v/f swap.
Same root as English 'greens' (vegetables). Groente comes from groen (green).
Same as English 'fruit'.
Same root as English 'apple'. Appel = apple.
Sinaas (Chinese) + appel (apple). An orange is literally a 'Chinese apple'!
Same as English 'banana'.
Aard (earth) + appel (apple). A potato is literally an 'earth apple'! French 'pomme de terre' means the same.
Same as English 'rice'. From the same Asian root.
Same as English 'pasta'.
Same root as English 'soup'. Soep = soup.
Same as English 'salad'. From Latin 'sal' (salt).
Same root as English 'butter'. Boter = butter.

sentences.dutch: Wil je suiker in je thee?
sentences.english: Do you want sugar in your tea?

note: Same root as English 'sugar'. Suiker = sugar.
Same root as English 'salt'. Zout = salt. The z/s swap.
Same root as English 'pepper'. Peper = pepper.

sentences.dutch: Ik eet ontbijt om acht uur.
sentences.english: I eat breakfast at eight o'clock.

note: Ont means 'un-' and bijten means 'to bite'. Un-bite = break-fast! Same logic as English.

sentences.english: I eat lunch at the office.

note: Same as English 'lunch'.
Avond (evening) + eten (food). Literally 'evening-food' = dinner.

sentences.dutch: We ontmoeten elkaar in het café.
sentences.english: We meet each other in the café.

note: Same as English 'café'. From French.
Same root as English 'which'. Welk = which.

sentences.dutch: Ik ga slapen, want ik ben moe.
sentences.english: I'm going to sleep, for I am tired.

note: Same root as old English 'want' (lacking). Want = because/for.

sentences.dutch: Het regent, dus ik blijf thuis.
sentences.english: It's raining, so I stay home.

note: Same root as English 'thus'. Dus = so/therefore.

sentences.dutch: Ik denk dat het goed is.

note: Same root as English 'that'. Dat = that.

sentences.dutch: Toen ik jong was, speelde ik voetbal.
sentences.english: When I was young, I played soccer.

note: Same root as English 'then'. Toen = when (past)/then.
Ter (at the) + wijl (while). Same root as English 'while'. Terwijl = while.

sentences.dutch: Hoewel het regent, ga ik naar buiten.
sentences.english: Although it's raining, I go outside.

note: Hoe (how) + wel (well). Literally 'how well' = although. Acknowledging something is true but...

sentences.dutch: Ik studeer zodat ik kan slagen.
sentences.english: I study so that I can pass.

note: Zo (so) + dat (that). Literally 'so that'. Identical logic to English.

sentences.dutch: De tuin is achter het huis.
sentences.english: The garden is behind the house.

note: Same root as English 'after'. Achter = behind/after.

sentences.english: I sit next to my friend.

note: Na (near/after) + ast. Same root as English 'next/nigh'. Naast = next to.
Same root as English 'cost'. Kosten = to cost.

sentences.dutch: De film eindigt om tien uur.

Af (off/fixed) + spraak (speech). Literally 'fixed speech/agreement' = appointment.

Ge (together) + sprek (speak). A gesprek is speaking together = conversation.

Same root as English 'name'. Naam = name.

Leef (live) + tijd (time). Literally 'life-time' = age.

From zorgen (to care/worry). Bezorgd literally means 'be-worried' - worried about something!
